newsitem.title: USA: Florida cop cleared in shooting that sparked riot.
newsitem.headline: Florida cop cleared in shooting that sparked riot.

text.p: A Florida grand jury ruled on Wednesday that a white police officer was justified in shooting a young black motorist whose death sparked a night of rioting.
"We have determined the death of Tyron Lewis was the result of a justifiable homicide under Florida law," Pinellas County State Attorney Bernie McCabe said after the 16-member grand jury acted.

The decision prompted fears of more violence in St. Petersburg, where the police department had assigned officers to patrol in teams during the day in preparation for the ruling. Community leaders appealed for calm.

The fatal shooting of Lewis, 18, during what seemed a routine traffic stop on Oct. 24 was followed by hours of rioting in south St. Petersburg, a predominantly black section of this western Florida city.
At least 11 people were hurt, mostly police officers, and nearly 30 fires were set in shops, businesses and homes before police regained control early the next morning.

The grand jury ruled the death of Lewis was justifiable homicide because officer James Knight, who shot Lewis, was in danger of being run over by the car Lewis was driving after he and his partner, Sandra Minor, pulled Lewis over for speeding.

Black youths in the city charged they were constantly victimised by police. Community leaders said poverty, lack of jobs and bleak prospects for African Americans in St. Petersburg created resentment that fuelled the unrest. The incident also prompted federal investigations.
Knight, 34, appeared before the grand jury on Tuesday to provide his account. He has been on administrative leave since the shooting.
Minor, who was one of the first witnesses to testify in the case, returned on Tuesday to testify a second time.
